description: Two independent LFOs whose wave morphs from sine to square, each playing only the part of the cycle between a start point and an end point, and each able to lock to a clock

params.text: Sets the frequency of that channel's LFO, 0.0001Hz to 2Hz at slow, 1Hz to 20Hz at med and 18Hz to 80Hz at fast; while the channel is synced it divides the synced rate instead, by 16 down to 1
Morphs the shape of that channel's wave from sine through triangle to saw, and most of the way to a square at the top of its travel
Sets the point in the cycle at which that channel's wave begins; while the channel is synced this steps through nine positions rather than sweeping
Sets the point in the cycle at which that channel's wave wraps back to its start point; while the channel is synced this steps through nine positions rather than sweeping
Chooses the frequency band that channel's Rate knob covers, slow, med or fast, and the multiple of the synced tempo used while the channel is synced

inputs.text: Adds to that channel's Rate knob, 5V covering the knob's whole travel, with the total clamped at the ends of that travel
Adds to that channel's Morph knob, 5V covering the knob's whole travel, with the total clamped at the ends of that travel
Adds to that channel's Start knob, 5V covering the knob's whole travel, with the total clamped at the ends of that travel
Adds to that channel's End knob, 5V covering the knob's whole travel, with the total clamped at the ends of that travel
A rising edge here syncs that channel, taking its rate from the interval between edges, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge here sets that channel's phase back to its start point, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V

outputs.text: 10V for 2000 samples each time that channel's wave reaches its end point and wraps back to the start point, and 0V the rest of the time

notes: With End set below Start the wave runs backwards through the cycle, and with the two within a hundredth of each other the phase stops moving and the output holds.
A channel stays synced only while edges keep arriving at its Sync input; one second after the last edge it goes back to the rate its Rate knob and speed switch set.
The synced rate is averaged over the last four intervals between Sync edges, so a tempo change takes a few edges to settle.
